clue.text: Bill about to enter woodland that's divine

indicators.note: the reversed bill goes into the middle of the woodland word

parts.note: a forest is woodland

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the word for bill round

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: An invoice somehow finds its way into a sacred grove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like the adjective 'holy', but here it is the verb meaning to foretell.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to predict or foresee, as a weather prediction foresees what is coming.

clue.text: Fragile insect around is getting maiden hiding

indicators.note: the insect word wraps around the rest

parts.note: a fly is an insect

indicators.note: the word is conceals the maiden letter inside it

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A delicate bug flits about, keeping a young woman out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' has 'is' conceal the maiden; 'around' then wraps the insect round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flimsy is weak and easily broken, a synonym for fragile.

clue.text: Bank inadequate — this person's experience for a second time

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to bank on is to rely
this person is the speaker, I, so this person's = I have, I'VE

explanation.surface: Someone admits their savings fall short of what they have been through.
explanation.walkthrough: RELY cut short by 'inadequate' gives REL; 'this person's' is read as 'I have', I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: To live through an event again, in memory or in fact, is a repeat of the experience.

clue.text: Conservative is on adventure to achieve victorious outcome

parts.note: a quest is an adventurous expedition

explanation.surface: A Tory sets off on an exploit hoping to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquest is a win over an enemy, the result of being victorious.

clue.text: Band of specially trained troops on top of hotel

indicators.note: in a down answer, the troops sit above the hotel letter

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, an elite British army regiment
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A unit of special forces lands on a hotel roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: Make sense of marine unit

definitions.meaning: a measure of six feet used for the depth of water

explanation.surface: Trying to understand a measurement used at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means grasp or comprehend; the noun is a nautical depth measure of six feet.

clue.text: Old boys in maul after reunion

indicators.note: the letters are reunited in a new arrangement, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Former pupils pile into a rugby maul once their reunion is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after reunion' shuffles the letters of IN MAUL. A maul is a rugby scrum of players.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumni are former students of a school or college, old boys being the British term.

clue.text: Give one award for playing for being put at a disadvantage

parts.note: to hand is to give
I is the Roman numeral one
a cap is awarded to a player chosen for a national team

explanation.surface: A player is honoured with a prize, only to be penalised for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To handicap someone is to hamper them, putting them at a disadvantage.

clue.text: Traduced mum showing furrowed brow, we hear?

indicators.note: signals that the word is said aloud

parts.note: mum is MA, and a furrowed brow is LINED, together MA LINED

explanation.surface: A mother frowns after being spoken badly of.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce is to slander, speaking ill of someone unjustly.

clue.text: Funny chap Eric brought to head for indolence

parts.note: Eric Idle is a comedian from Monty Python
a ness is a headland, as in Orford Ness on the Suffolk coast

explanation.surface: A comedian is called before the boss for laziness.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS, a headland, appears in British place names such as Orford Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolence is laziness, the state of doing nothing.

clue.text: Pipe in underground passage changed at the entrance

indicators.note: the first letter of the passage word is swapped for another

parts.note: a tunnel is an underground passage

explanation.surface: A pipe runs through a subway that has been altered at its mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A funnel is a tube or chimney, such as a ship's smoke pipe.

clue.text: City offering quiet repose? No, upset!

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music
rest is repose

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word upside down

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a quiet lie-down and refuses angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESTON is a city in Lancashire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a Lancashire city, so an example of a city.

clue.text: Holy group beginning to voice our relish

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army, a church group

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word supplies only its first letter

explanation.surface: A church choir starts to sing with gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: To savour something is to enjoy it with relish.

clue.text: Moving with aim to settle in Herts town

indicators.note: the aim word lodges inside the town name

parts.note: Tring is a town in Hertfordshire, a county north of London
an end is an aim

explanation.surface: Someone relocates, hoping to make a home in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: TRING is a small market town in Hertfordshire (Herts), north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Trending means going or heading in a certain direction, so on the move.

clue.text: Trip in vessel ending in Greece with happiness spreading round

indicators.note: the happiness word spreads around the rest

parts.note: joy is happiness
an urn is a vessel

indicators.note: only the last letter of the country is used

explanation.surface: A holiday ends in Greece with a pot and lots of good cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey is a trip from one place to another.

clue.text: Unnatural pose to employ in embrace

indicators.note: an unnatural pose is an awkward arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to use is to employ

explanation.surface: A model strikes an awkward posture to use in a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt or embrace it.

clue.text: Money put down — little time to waste for Oriental drink

indicators.note: the time letter is wasted, lost from the word

parts.note: a stake is money laid as a bet
T is short for time

explanation.surface: A gambler loses money and no time drinking in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: STAKE loses T to give the Japanese rice wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sake is a Japanese rice wine, an alcoholic drink from the Far East.

clue.text: Always getting caught in police trap, manoeuvring car?

indicators.note: the word for always is trapped inside the police trap

parts.note: a sting is an undercover police trap
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A driver is forever caught in a police sting, dodging about.
explanation.walkthrough: EER is e'er, a poetic form of ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Steering is directing a car, guiding its movement; the question mark marks this as a definition by example.

clue.text: Seductive females full of anger — they want blood!

indicators.note: the seductive females word is filled with the anger word

parts.note: vamps are seductive women
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Furious femmes fatales thirsting for blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Vampires are creatures of folklore that drink human blood.

clue.text: Bird — that which covers short distance

indicators.note: the that-which word covers the short distance by going around it

parts.note: what means that which, as in 'what I said'
an inch is a short distance

explanation.surface: A bird cannot fly far.
explanation.definitionFit: The whinchat is a small songbird of the chat family.

clue.text: What curiously is the opposite of 22?

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the letters are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: Asking what the opposite of another answer is.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is FREEZE; its opposite is a melting.
explanation.definitionFit: A melting of ice is the reverse of a frost setting in.

clue.text: Commanding officer with onset of hunger tucked into cheese roll

indicators.note: the officer and the hunger letter are placed inside the cheese

parts.note: brie is a French cheese
OC is officer commanding

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hungry officer tucks into a cheese roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A brioche is a sweet French bread, often baked as a roll.

clue.text: From what we hear, discharges stop abruptly

indicators.note: signals that the word is said aloud

parts.note: frees means discharges or releases

explanation.surface: Rumours suggest someone releases things and then halts.
explanation.definitionFit: To come suddenly to a dead halt is to stay motionless, like a person stopped in their tracks.

clue.text: Sheep falling over trap in border area

indicators.note: in a down clue the sheep word is turned upside down

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a gin is an animal snare

explanation.surface: A sheep tumbles over a snare in the borderlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is an edge or border region of a page or space.

clue.text: Victoria describes one drunkard

definitions.meaning: a Victoria is a kind of cake, so the name describes the cake
a heavy drinker who soaks up alcohol

explanation.surface: A woman named Victoria calls someone a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: A Victoria sponge is a classic British jam-and-cream layer cake.
explanation.definitionFit: The cake named after Queen Victoria; also a slang word for someone who drinks to excess.

clue.text: Sort of business person no longer given beer

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A trader who has given up is handed a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An exporter is a trader who sells goods abroad, a kind of businessperson.

clue.text: Settle down temporarily in enclosure with a politician

parts.note: enc is the abbreviation for an enclosure in a letter
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician sets up camp in a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosure' looks like a pen but is the letter abbreviation enc.
explanation.definitionFit: To encamp is to set up a camp, staying somewhere for a short time.

clue.text: Ms Blyton turns up to have a meal

indicators.note: in a down clue the name is turned upside down

parts.note: Enid Blyton was a children's author

explanation.surface: A famous author arrives for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to eat a meal, especially dinner.

clue.text: Country artist starts to enjoy landscape on far side of island

indicators.note: the artist and the starting letters come after the island

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: the starts of the two words give their first letters

explanation.surface: A painter begins to enjoy the scenery beyond an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: Fellow hugging one companion, soldier going round American state

indicators.note: the fellow word hugs the rest inside it

parts.note: a man is a fellow
I is the Roman numeral one
CH is a Companion of Honour

indicators.note: going round turns the soldier word back to front

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A man embraces a friend while a soldier circles.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, a Companion of Honour, is a British honour often used for 'companion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Michigan is a US state in the Great Lakes region.

clue.text: Good American, he had demonstrated sentimentality

parts.note: US is American
he'd is short for he had

explanation.surface: A nice American man had been getting soppy.
explanation.definitionFit: To gush is to speak with excessive emotion or effusive feeling.

clue.text: Despatched from 'ere in a few words?

parts.note: sent means despatched
hence means from here; dropping the H as in 'ere gives 'ence

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks if a message was posted from here.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ere drops the H, so 'hence' (from here) becomes 'ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is a group of words expressing a complete thought.
